title: Human-trained neural model predicts regulatory maps across 447 mammalian genomes
summary: Using an experimentally mapped human atlas of 5.33 million regulatory elements from 4,159 samples, researchers trained a cell-context-informed neural sequence model. It predicted cell-selective accessibility, generalized to observed mouse data and was applied to predict regulatory activity across 447 mammalian genomes. The human atlas was measured experimentally, while the broad cross-species maps remain computational predictions without validation in every species. Zenodo metadata dates this preprint November 20, 2026; the version record was created November 21, which does not establish a November 20 archive posting.
ai_technology: LegNet-based convolutional sequence model with transcription-factor-repertoire cell-context embeddings

evidence.tested: Sequence model assessed on held-out human biosamples, unseen ATAC-seq samples and mouse data; model reportedly identified the highest-activity cell type for ~85% of cell-selective DHSs.
evidence.unknown: Predictions are not experimentally confirmed in all 447 species. Concept DOI10.5281/zenodo.24208043 and version DOI10.5281/zenodo.24208044 describe the same work; metadata publication date2026-11-20 differs from archive-record creation2026-11-21.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning sequence-to-activity model, trained on the Atlas, predicts cell-selective regulatory DNA actuation from sequence and generalizes the predictions to mammalian genomes.
